title: Natural Domain and Range of a Rational Function
originalTopic: Functions and Graphs: Natural Domain and Range
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Find the natural domain and range of the rational function defined by f(t) = 4 / (3 - t).

steps.title: Identify Denominator Singularities
steps.explanation: In any rational function, division by zero is undefined. Setting the denominator 3 - t != 0 requires excluding t = 3.
steps.why: Division by zero is undefined in the real number system.

steps.title: Formulate the Domain in Interval Notation
steps.explanation: All real numbers t except t = 3 yield a valid quotient, partitioning the domain into two open intervals.
steps.why: Removing a single point from the real line leaves the union of two disjoint open rays.

steps.title: Invert the Relation to Find the Range
steps.explanation: Set y = 4 / (3 - t) and solve for t in terms of y. The resulting expression t = 3 - 4/y produces a valid real number t != 3 for every real number y except y = 0.
steps.why: A value y belongs to the range if and only if the equation f(t) = y has at least one solution t in the domain.

steps.title: State the Range in Interval Notation
steps.explanation: Because the numerator 4 is non-zero, the fraction can never equal 0, while taking all other real values as t varies across (-inf, 3) U (3, inf).
steps.why: A fraction with a constant non-zero numerator never vanishes and approaches +/-infinity near its vertical asymptote.
